title: Contract Regression Fuzzbench and Client Signal Harness
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Build a reusable harness that runs contract fuzzing and shadow/dual runs across API versions to detect regressions when we change streaming, tool/function calling, or structured output behavior. This ticket implements the server-side orchestration, golden corpus, and CI integration so that incoming PRs that touch protocol shaping, behavior flags, or kernel scheduling are automatically probed against representative client signals.
goals: Create a fuzzbench that can generate realistic client signal permutations for streaming + tool calls + structured outputs
Run dual/shadow executions (old-version vs candidate-version) at scale and collect diffs in a standardized format
Surface high-confidence regressions to the Console and create alertable dashboards
Provide a reproducible bundle for engineering (inputs + seed + server flags) for triage
Add a gated CI job that fails if regression score exceeds threshold and auto-opens a regression artifact PR
acceptance_criteria: Fuzzbench runs end-to-end in CI (nightly + PR) and produces a regression summary artifact
We can reproduce any flagged regression locally via a generated repro bundle within 10 minutes
Telemetry emits per-run metrics: delta_score, token_error_rate, toolcall_mismatch_rate, structured-json-schema-diff_count
Policy: any P1 regression (delta_score > 0.15 on golden set) blocks merge and files a ticket in Linear
Documentation: migration guide updated with 'how to interpret fuzzbench output' and example handler code
Console dashboard shows top 10 impacted customers/tenants for surfaced regressions (anonymized until triage)
test_plan: Assemble golden corpus covering: short prompts, long-streaming dialogs, nested tool-call sequences, and structured-output templates
Instrument client SDKs to emit canonical signal set (headers + streaming frames + toolcall metadata + expected_schema) via test-mode flag
Run dual-execution harness: baseline (runtime-1.18) vs candidate (PR artifact). Capture token-level diffs and toolcall side-effects
Score outputs with a configurable comparator chain: exact-json-check -> schema-aware-levenshtein -> semantic-embedding-distance
Threshold evaluation: map comparator outputs to delta_score and run alerting rules
On failure, publish repro bundle (input seed, model config, behavior flags) plus a short-run recording to S3 and open ENG ticket automatically
implementation_notes: Prefer server-side harness that spins ephemeral containers to avoid bias from local dev environments
Initial comparator will focus on structural mismatches for toolcall ordering and explicit failure codes; add semantic checks later
Keep corpus extensible: store as versioned artifacts in GCS with metadata tags (api_version, scenario, author)
To reduce cost, use adaptive sampling: run full golden set nightly and a trimmed smoke set on PRs
Integrate with existing rollout/fallback policy so that a candidate that fails can auto-fallback to baseline for live traffic while engineers triage
decisions: Decision 1: Use dual-run comparison (baseline vs candidate) rather than replay-only — gives direct delta signals and isolates server-side changes
Decision 2: Start with deterministic fuzzing seeds derived from production anonymized prompts; do not sample raw production traffic into CI to avoid PII
Decision 3: Scoring pipeline uses weighted comparators: (toolcall_mismatch 0.5, structured_schema_diff 0.3, semantic_distance 0.2). We can tune weights after first month
Decision 4: Behavior flags will be tested explicitly by enumerating flag permutations for critical flags; non-critical flags are sampled
Decision 5: Block merges for high-confidence regressions; low-confidence regressions will create non-blocking alerts with triage assignment
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives from semantic comparator — Mitigation: require corroborating structural mismatch or toolcall mismatch before blocking
Risk: CI cost spike from running full corpus — Mitigation: adaptive sampling and cache reuse across similar PRs
Risk: Overfitting to golden set — Mitigation: rotate corpus monthly and include randomized seeds
Risk: Leaking customer data — Mitigation: use anonymized, synthetic corpus and strip tokens before storing repro bundles
